title: Exercise 1: Calculating the concentration of a commercial hydrochloric acid solution
body:
Commercial hydrochloric acid is supplied as a solution containing 37 % hydrochloric acid by mass.

Data: Molar mass: M(HCl) = 36.46 g·mol-1

Density: ρ(commercial HCl) = 1.19 g·cm-3

The print command.

The syntax for using the print command is:

print(a)

To display a string, use quotation marks (''). You can also ask Python to display a result in scientific notation and/or with a specified number of decimal places using f-strings. Specifying the number of decimal places:

print(f"{a:.2f}")

Here, 2 is the number of decimal places and f specifies fixed-point notation. Scientific notation with a specified number of decimal places:

print(f"{a:.2E}")

The E format uses scientific notation. Variables. A variable is assigned using the = sign (for example, a=2). Be careful with letter case: Python distinguishes uppercase and lowercase letters.

Instructions:

1. Write a Python program to calculate the molar concentration of hydrochloric acid in this solution. Define the data and the calculation formula using variables.

2. Display the result using the print command.

title: Exercise 2: Calculating the pH of a diluted hydrochloric acid solution
body:
The commercial hydrochloric acid solution at 12.076 mol·L-1 is now diluted. Take 166 μL of the stock solution and make up to 100 mL with distilled water.

The def statement (function)

A function is defined using the following structure:

def nom_de_la_fonction(variable1, variable2):
    # Instructions de calcul
    return resultat

The logarithm function

The base-10 logarithm is not a built-in Python function. You need to use the math module. You have three options:

1. Import the entire module:

import math

2. Import a specific function:

from math import log10

3. Use an alias:

import math as m

Instructions:

1. Calculate the pH of the diluted solution in two ways:

• By defining the concentration as a variable.

• By defining a function.

2. Display:

• The concentration of the diluted solution in scientific notation with two decimal places.

• The pH value with two decimal places.

title: Exercise 3: Calculating the pH of a formic acid solution
body:
Unlike a strong acid, a weak acid dissociates only partially in water. The equilibrium constant for this dissociation is called the acid dissociation constant, Ka. Given: pKa(HCOOH/HCOO−) = 3.75. Solving the quadratic equation: Write a function deg2(a, b, c) to solve the equation, taking the following three cases into account:

• Δ>0: Two real solutions; retain the positive value.

• Δ=0: One real solution.

• Δ<0: No real solution. Handle these three cases using a conditional structure.

Conditional statements (if ... elif ... else)

A conditional structure lets you handle different cases depending on the input variable. It uses if, elif (short for

else if), and else. Within a function, you can write:

if condition_1:
    return resultat_1
elif condition_2:
    return resultat_2
else:
    return resultat_3

Instructions:

1. Determine the equilibrium pH of a formic acid solution at 2.00⋅10−3 mol·L−1 by solving the quadratic equation.

title: Exercise 4: Predominance diagram for formic acid
body:
As the pH increases, formic acid loses a proton to form the formate ion. The graph showing the percentage of the two species as a function of pH is called a predominance diagram.

Given: [HCOOH] = 2.00 × 10-3 mol·L-1

The for loop. A for loop can use a starting value and an excluded end value to define

the range over which it repeats. Using in range defines an interval [a,b[ and a step size. If the step is omitted, it defaults to 1. It can be increased but must be an integer. The syntax of a for loop is:

for i in range (début, fin exclue) :

statement(s). The loop stops when the end value is reached, but the successive values are not automatically saved. To retain them, you can use a list, which has the advantage of being mutable.

Mutable lists.

First define an empty list (x_a=[]), then add the loop values to the list with the append method (x_a.append(a)). The syntax is:

x_a = []
x_a.append(valeur)

The matplotlib.pyplot module

To create a graph, import the module:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

Plot a curve using:

plt.plot(x, y, color='blue', linestyle='-', linewidth=2, label='Courbe')

color (or c) = ‘...’ sets the line colour; linestyle (or ls) = ‘…’ sets the line style (dotted ‘:’, dashed ‘--’); linewidth (or lw) = number sets the line width; label = ‘...’ sets the legend entry for the curve. Graph settings: Add a title and axis labels:

plt.title('Titre')
plt.xlabel('Nom axe X')
plt.ylabel('Nom axe Y')
plt.legend() # afficher la légende défini dans les paramètres

The legend entries are defined in the plotting parameters.

plt.show() # demander à Python de faire le graphique

Instructions:

1. Create three lists containing:

• The pH values.

• The percentage of formic acid.

• The percentage of formate ions.

2. Use a for loop to calculate the percentages of the acid and base species for pH values between 0 and 14, and store them in lists. Have your program display the resulting lists.

3. Plot the percentages of the acid and base forms of formic acid as a function of pH. Use two different colours to distinguish the species. Choose different markers for the two plots and an appropriate marker size. The graph must have a title and clearly labelled axes, and the two forms must be easy to identify.
